title: Two views, one object
hook: Two viewpoints do not see precisely the same image.

knows: Animals have structures and behaviors suited to particular conditions.
doesNotKnow: The dot sits in different positions in the two schematic views. Differences between the eyes’ images can contribute to binocular depth perception; the picture is not a measurement and other visual cues can also support depth judgments.

misconception: A familiar animal behavior or structure must work in a different way.
objective: When two forward-facing eyes view one nearby object, what visual difference can help estimate depth?
